notes:
CRM notes and call snippets:
- Account: Elmwood Systems & Analytics (global travel booking + personalization). Heavy peak-season throughput (flash sales).
- Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with strict SLA for uptime + latency SLOs. Must support VPC peering to EU region and on-prem sync for sensitive PII workloads.
- Throughput targets: baseline commitment 200k tokens/minute steady, burst to 600k tokens/min when promotions run. Expect sustained 150-200 qps for real-time personalization endpoints.
- Latency SLOs: 95th pct tail latency target <= 250ms for chat/rerank; median <100ms. Will require TTFP and token latency profiling.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial reserved pool = 8 A100 equiv for POC -> staging target 16 -> production commit 40 by 2026-05-01. Need clear timeline and provisioning lead times in contract.
- SLA negotiation points highlighted by Elmwood legal:
  * Uptime target: Elmwood requests 99.99% (target) but will accept 99.95% with stronger credits.
  * Credit schedule ask: Propose progressive credits: 99.95-99.99 = 10% monthly credit; 99.9-99.95 = 25% credit; <99.9 = 50% credit + right to terminate after two consecutive months. Elmwood pushing for credits to be applied against committed reserved fees (not just pay-as-you-go).
  * Maintenance windows: Elmwood requires scheduled maintenance limited to quarterly 2-hour windows, with 30-day advance notice; no maintenance allowed during pre-declared promotional blackout windows (5-day windows around major sales).
  * Support SLAs: P1 response <= 15 minutes, P2 <= 1 hour, P3 <= 4 hours; 24/7 on-call for P1 incidents, direct escalation path to infra engineering.
  * Data residency & audit: All audit logs must be retained 12 months and delivered on-demand; KMS integration mandatory for key material.
- Redwood points: offering 99.95% standard for Dedicated with enhanced plan for 99.99% (requires replication across AZs/regions). Standard credit schedule currently: <99.95 => escalating credits up to 30% on reserved fees. Need to adapt wording to Elmwood's ask.
- POC findings: under the test workload, caching + batching reduced token cost by ~18% and improved throughput. Quantization trial deferred — Elmwood concerned about slight regression in NLG quality at certain quantization levels.
- Quote discussion: Elmwood wants credits applied to reserved monthly commit. Also wants explicit provisioning SLA (time-to-provision new GPUs within 14 days of written request up to agreed cap).
- Legal: asked for a clause that allows partial service credits for sustained partial degradations (e.g., increased p95 latency). Asking Redwood for a clear latency SLO measurement method (reporting window, measurement agent, synthetic vs real traffic).
- SE notes: measure p95 with 95th token latency across customer-defined endpoints, exclude scheduled maintenance and force-majeure; need to agree on instrumentation (Redwood tracing + Elmwood synthetic probes).
- Quote status: draft sent 2026-03-11 to elmwood-legal (thread-CAoXk9j-elmwood-sla-negotiation).
- Tone: pragmatic but tough negotiating — Elmwood has enterprise procurement counsel and strict blackout windows. They value predictable capacity and credits applied to committed spend.
- Direct quote: "We cannot risk our sale event going down for 20 minutes — that loses millions. We need contractual guarantees and operational playbooks." — Elmwood Head of Engineering (call 2026-03-02).
